item.description:

item.description: ජනාධිපති අනුර කුමාර දිසානායක මහතා හදිසි අසනීප තත්ත්වයක් හේතුවෙන් පෞද්ගලික රෝහලකට ඇතුළත් කර ඇති බවට සමාජ මාධ්‍ය ඔස්සේ ඊයේ (24) ව්‍යාජ ප්‍රචාරයක් යවා තිබූ අතර මෙම ආරංචිය කෙතරම් දුර පැතිරගියේද යත් එය අසත්‍ය බවට ජනපති මාධ්‍ය අංශයෙන් නිල නිවේදනයක් නිකුත් කිරීමට තරම් හේතුවක් විය. මෙම ප්‍රචාරය එක්තරා දේශපාලන කණ්ඩායමක් මගින් සමාජ මාධ්‍ය වෙත යොමු කර ඇති බවටත් එයට පසුබිම් වන්නේ ‍'මැටි බෝනික්කංට කටු ගැසීමේ' මිථ්‍යා දෘෂ්ඨික යාගයක ප්‍රතිඵල ලැබුණ බවට එම කණ්ඩායමේ පාක්ෂිකයන්ට ඒත්තු ගන්වා සතුටක් ලබාදීමට බවත් මේ

item.description: The Daily FT - ACCA and the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka, together with WIM, the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors, the MBA Alumni Association of the University of Colombo and Pioneer Institute of Business & Technology, will be conducting their milestone 50th webinar.

item.title: [Daily FT - Business/Sectors] Treasury hails Sri Lanka Customs’ contributions to recovery, development
item.description: Treasury Secretary Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma has hailed Sri Lanka Customs’ (SLC) contributions to the country’s recovery and development, saying revenue collected by the department enabled the Government to allocate Rs. 500 billion to respond to the Ditwah disaster and to provide relief on fuel prices driven up by the war in the Middle East.

item.title: [Daily FT - Business/Sectors] Welfare net fails to track household shocks: IPS
item.description: Sri Lanka’s social protection system reaches households regardless of how exposed they are to shocks, the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) said. This leaves many of the poorest and most shock-hit households without support.

item.title: [Daily FT - Business/Sectors] Tourist arrivals rise 5% in first 22 days of October
item.description: Sri Lanka welcomed 119,805 tourists during the first 22 days of October, registering a 5.03% year-on-year (YoY) increase, but cumulative arrivals remained 1.42% below the corresponding period last year as the industry entered its crucial winter season.

item.title: [Daily FT - Business/Sectors] CSE falls 2.48% during week
item.description: The Colombo stock market continued to slide for a fifth straight session to end the week in the red. During the week, the ASPI fell 2.48% and the active S&P SL20 fell 2.18% as intensifying tensions in the Middle East fed into negative investor sentiment.
